Hi Neha,

1) Confirmation that a Dedicated deployment can be strictly pinned to a single AWS region for our tenant (we plan to use us-west-2).
2) Evidence that ephemeral artifacts (KV cache, request logs, batching buffers) are not replicated out of region and can be purged on demand.
3) A simple attestation we can attach to our SOC/supplier review showing the wipe process and timelines.

Hi Alex — thanks for the clear list. Looping in Marissa (Product Ops) and Dev (Infra) to provide the artifacts and the operational details. Quick answers before they jump in: 

- Yes — Dedicated tenants can be region-pinned (single region host). We operate tenant placement at provisioning and do not move tenant compute between regions without an explicit customer migration request.
- Ephemeral runtime state (KV caches, batching buffers) lives on local SSD-backed VMs on the pinned region and is not asynchronously replicated by default.
- Backups: persistent backups can be configured; the standard Dedicated backup cadence for this class is nightly snapshots. Those snapshots respect the tenant region and are stored in the same region unless the customer opts into cross-region replication (opt-in only).

I'll attach the high-level dataflow diagram and our region-pin checklist. Marissa will follow with the wipe attestation template and the step-by-step purge runbook. Dev, can you confirm retention windows for ephemeral caches and the SLA on wipe completion after a pin removal request?

Attachments: redwood-dedicated-dataflow-diagram.pdf, region-pin-checklist.xlsx

Best,
Neha Kapoor

Hi Alex — following up with the runbook and attestation details. I pulled together a short playbook and a template attestation we can sign once we complete validation in your environment. Highlights below and link to the secure folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2B3cDummyLink

- Region pinning: provisioning creates tenant resources in a single region (us-west-2). Network ACLs and VPC routing are scoped to that AZ/region. We record the region assignment in the tenant metadata and expose it in the Console and audit logs.
- Ephemeral state: KV cache/worker caches are persisted on local ephemeral storage. Evictions occur continuously; to meet an on-demand wipe request we run a two-pass process: 1) in-memory flush/clear + disk trim; 2) mark-for-deletion and scrub any local snapshots. This process is described in the attached runbook.
- Backups: our standard Dedicated backup job creates EBS snapshots once daily. By default snapshots are region-local. Snapshots are retained for 30 days unless you request a shorter retention. If you request immediate deletion, we can schedule expedited snapshot deletion — timeline depends on AWS snapshot lifecycle but we commit to initiating deletion within 4 hours of an approved wipe request and providing evidence when deletion completes.

Attached: tenant-wipe-attestation-template.pdf (fillable), redwood-dedicated-dataflow-diagram.pdf, region-pin-checklist.xlsx

If helpful we can produce an attestation signed by Product Ops and send our ops runbook excerpt (hashed) to your auditors. Typical deliverables:
- Signed attestation PDF tailored to the tenant (we populate tenant name, region, and the request timestamp)
- Audit log excerpt showing region pin metadata and provisioning event
- Signed deletion confirmation once scrub completes

I can also redact internal IPs and include only the metadata fields your auditors need. What format does your supplier review prefer? PDF attestation + CSV of audit events?

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Sr. Product Ops Manager

Alex — answers inline and next steps: 

- KV cache TTL and scrub: TTL controls in-memory eviction. For on-disk artifacts we run the two-pass scrub even if TTL > 0 when a formal wipe request is issued. Dev — confirm we capture the wipe job completion timestamp in audit logs (yes/no).
- Worst-case deletion window: backups are subject to cloud provider snapshot deletion semantics. Our commitment: we will initiate deletion within 4 hours of authorization; worst-case completion for snapshot lifecycle purge is up to 72 hours in practice (we record and deliver the snapshot deletion confirmation). We will include the upper-bound language in the attestation.
- Signed attestation contact: Marissa Cole, Sr. Product Ops Manager (marissa_cole@redwood.ai).
